description: First deterministic source/author curation layer for poetry_corpus_v0_source_native_accepted_candidate. Conservative by design: merge obvious duplicate poet identities, reject rows with artifact flags, reject non-author/editor/translator/classical-translation sources before pair derivation. v1 adds strict source-level OCR/artifact quarantines from experiment 026 data spotcheck. v2 adds heldout-specific source quarantines from v5.1 probe audit. v3 adds targeted row-level artifact cleanup after exp027 spotcheck: TOC/page-list rows, prefaces, transcriber notes, publisher ads/reviews, and source edition prose. v4 follows v5.3 probe audit: removes repeated italic title-list rows, obvious Brooke biography prose, remaining publisher/music adverts, and the Pope Leo XIII commentary/Latin bucket.

reject_text_regex: \b(first published|published in\s+\d{4}|published for the first time|included in\s+\d{4}|edition of\s+\d{4}|alteration since|altered and in some cases|practically unaltered)\b
\b(Published in Boston|published in the Transactions|American Philosophical Society)\b
\b(edited with textual notes|critical notes|editor'?s note|biography of the poet|the three generations of readers|literary men were|fellow-townswoman|note on text)\b
\b(crown 8vo|cloth,?\s*\d+mo|price \$|price \d+s|second edition|popular edition|full page illustrations|uniform in size and style)\b
\b(fcap\.?|fcp\.?|gilt leaves|bevelled boards|handsome cover|engravings by|new edition, revised|gazetteer of the world)\b
\b(corrections? and illustrations|commentators|chronological order|dissertation|lectures on the history|oxford reformers)\b
\b(notes on passages|modern language review|stanza\s+\d+\.\s*1\.\s*\d|mocking bird|natural note|favourite imitations)\b
\bOF the miscellaneous collection of verse that follows\b
\bThe "portfolios" were found, shortly after Emily Dickinson\'s death\b
\bOnly the most obvious punctuation errors repaired\b
\bOf sketches, poetical as well as pictorial\b
\bThis book is the realization of a plan\b
\bNearly half of the present volume has been\b
\bThe same kind of materials is used\b
\bTna authoress of this neat little volume\b
\bIt had been (?:ray|my) wish, on presenting the public\b
\bWe welcomthis volume as a graceful tribute\b
\bBoth poems are highly praised for their affectionateness\b
\bIt was a favorite project of the Pope\b
